analysis.title: Thoughts for 2027 - Investment version
key_insights: Higher yields have restored income as the main starting point for fixed income returns. Yields would need to rise meaningfully before total returns turn negative, while a modest fall in yields could produce strong capital gains.

Growth is expected to stay resilient, supported by AI capex and defence spending. Insight expects tighter financial conditions to weigh on interest-rate-sensitive areas, which could make restrictive policy harder to sustain and let the policy cycle turn faster than markets expect.

Inflation may moderate in the second half of 2027 if oil supplies normalise, but Insight does not expect a return to reliably low and stable inflation. Fragmentation, fragile supply chains, government spending and competition for energy and commodities could keep inflation structurally higher and more volatile.
Inflation-linked government bond yields have repriced and inflation-linked assets have cheapened. Insight sees this as a potential opportunity to add inflation protection.

Term premia have risen even at 10-year maturities despite higher short-term rates. Insight sees value in 10-year bonds across several markets, while 30-year bonds have become more volatile and depend on fiscal credibility.
The UK is one of few major economies planning fiscal consolidation. A credible shift in market perception of UK fiscal policy could benefit gilts.

Long-dated government bonds are a less dependable diversifier because inflation can force central banks to tighten as growth weakens, so equities and bonds can fall together. Government debt is near or above 100% of GDP in several developed economies.
Lower index duration, shown in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate, gives a larger income cushion but less capital gain potential when yields fall.

Options, commodities and currency strategies are proposed as supplementary diversifiers. Puts can protect against equity falls while keeping upside exposure. Commodities had a correlation of +0.2 with US equities and -0.2 with US government bonds over 1930-2026.

Rising Treasury issuance has increased the Treasury weight in the US Aggregate and reduced the corporate weight. That gives corporates technical support now, but corporates may need to pay a wider premium if government issuance keeps outpacing corporate issuance and yields rise.

AI infrastructure financing is a new source of credit supply. Large technology issuers have been absorbed comfortably so far, and Insight expects relative-value opportunities and the value of active security selection to grow in 2027.
Short-dated investment-grade and high-yield bonds, floating-rate credit and ABS can deliver income comparable to broader markets with lower rate sensitivity and lower volatility.

US tax-exempt municipal bonds offer taxable-equivalent yields above US investment grade beyond ten years for higher-rate taxpayers. About 67% of the municipal universe is rated AA or AAA versus under 9% of US investment-grade corporates.

Global high yield yields are back at 2024 levels. A sideways yield trend could deliver high single-digit returns, income should be the main driver, and high dispersion favours active selection. Lower-rated issuers may turn to private credit.

Emerging market debt saw broad inflows return in 2026. Insight is constructive on select local rates markets and on hard-currency debt, and sees emerging high-yield corporates as particularly attractive because the asset class has shrunk by about a third and net rating upgrades have been unusually strong.

US household assets have grown faster than federal debt, which supports the case for securitised assets. Wealth is unevenly distributed, so collateral, structure and security selection matter, and floating-rate ABS offer income without relying on tight corporate spreads.

Currency volatility is subdued and the trade-weighted dollar has traded broadly sideways. Insight is constructive on the Japanese yen and Swedish krona and expects greater currency dispersion and a greater need for hedging in 2027.

Structural themes to watch in 2027: EU securitisation reform, European pension reform, and digital assets. The GENIUS Act is expected to take effect on 18 January 2027, and the CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate in September 2026.

Risk to the central scenario: any concern about the sustainability of the AI investment boom could cause markets to reprice quickly with volatility rising, given that valuations reflect a benign outlook.

macro_indicators.indicator: Hyperscaler AI capex as % of US GDP
macro_indicators.reading: Above 2.5% in 2026, reaching 4% by 2028 (cumulative about 13% of GDP over five years)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports growth and is insensitive to interest rates, which makes restrictive policy harder to sustain.
Tailwind to European activity. NATO members are committed to 5% of GDP on defence and security by 2035.

macro_indicators.reading: No participant judged risks to growth tilted to the downside
macro_indicators.interpretation: Reflects high confidence in the US outlook, which leaves markets exposed to disappointment.

macro_indicators.reading: Expected to moderate in the second half of 2027 if oil supplies normalise
macro_indicators.interpretation: Inflation is expected to stay structurally higher and more volatile than before the pandemic.

macro_indicators.indicator: Estimated one-year returns, parallel yield shift
macro_indicators.reading: Based on yields at 30 October 2026, projected one year forward under +50bp, unchanged and -50bp scenarios
macro_indicators.interpretation: Income cushions a 50bp rise in yields for most fixed income asset classes, and a 50bp fall could give double-digit returns in some.
Europe's securitisation market is underdeveloped relative to the US, so reform has room to expand issuance.

crypto_views: 2027 could be an important test of whether greater regulatory certainty on digital assets leads to greater institutional adoption.
Tokenised money-market funds and deposits are the clearest early use cases, and tokenisation could extend to ETFs, private-market funds and underlying securities.
The US GENIUS Act puts stablecoins on a formal regulatory footing, with an expected effective date of 18 January 2027.
The CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate in September 2026, shifting responsibility to the SEC and CFTC to write rules under existing authorities.

trade_ideas.description: Add inflation-linked government bonds as inflation protection
trade_ideas.rationale: Inflation-linked government bond yields have repriced and the assets have cheapened.

trade_ideas.description: Own 10-year government bonds in markets where term premia have risen
trade_ideas.rationale: Insight sees value in 10-year bonds across several markets as term premia have risen.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated deficits and issuance could keep longer-dated bonds volatile.

trade_ideas.description: Short-dated investment-grade and high-yield credit, floating-rate credit and ABS for income
trade_ideas.rationale: They offer yields similar to broader markets with lower volatility and limited rate sensitivity.

trade_ideas.description: Long Japanese yen and Swedish krona currency positions
trade_ideas.rationale: Insight is constructive where carry, valuation and macro factors appear to be aligning.
trade_ideas.risk: Greater policy and political uncertainty elsewhere argues for selectivity.

trade_ideas.description: Emerging market hard-currency debt, particularly high-yield EM corporates, and select local rates
trade_ideas.rationale: The EM high-yield corporate universe has shrunk by about a third and net upgrades have been unusually strong.
trade_ideas.risk: Renewed inflation pressure and policy tightening in some countries require selectivity.

trade_ideas.description: AAA US municipal bonds beyond ten years for higher-rate taxpayers
trade_ideas.rationale: Taxable-equivalent yields are above US investment grade beyond ten years and above BB corporates in very long maturities.

trade_ideas.description: Buy put options on equities for portfolio protection
trade_ideas.rationale: Puts provide protection against equity falls while retaining exposure to gains.

risk_factors: Yields could rise further if central banks struggle to contain inflation expectations and tighten aggressively.
Wider credit spreads could weigh on credit returns.
Large government financing needs and AI-related corporate issuance could compete for capital and force corporates to pay wider spreads.
Fiscal credibility concerns could keep long-dated bonds volatile.
Equity-bond correlation could turn positive again, reducing the diversification value of bonds.
A concern about the sustainability of AI investment could trigger a rapid market repricing.
Wealth is unevenly distributed in the US, so lower-income consumers are more exposed to higher borrowing costs, which matters for ABS collateral.
Lower-rated high-yield issuers may struggle to refinance in public markets.
charts_described: Figure 3 plots AI capex as a share of US GDP, with September 2026 forecasts above November 2025 forecasts and 4% by 2028.
Figure 5 shows no FOMC members seeing downside risks to growth.
Figure 12 shows the 12-month rolling correlation between MSCI World and the Bloomberg Global Aggregate rising over time, with bonds a less reliable diversifier since the pandemic.
vol_and_positioning: Currency volatility is subdued, and a rise in currency volatility or a decisive dollar breakout from its range would make hedging benefits apparent quickly.
Markets could reprice quickly with volatility rising if concerns emerge about the sustainability of AI investment.
Put options can protect against equity falls while retaining upside, and other structures trade upside participation for protection or income.
About 100bp-plus dispersion in high yield remains reasonably high, which favours security selection.
geopolitical: Disruption to the Strait of Hormuz in 2026 produced shortages, higher input costs and inflationary pressure, and European oil inventories will take time to rebuild after the conflict is resolved.
Strategic competition between major powers across energy, critical minerals, semiconductors, shipping routes and financial infrastructure.
Broad US tariffs and conflict in the Middle East were among the shocks the global economy has absorbed.
NATO members committed to reaching 5% of GDP on core defence and broader security spending by 2035.

tension_points.bull_case: AI capex and defence spending are rate-insensitive and keep growth resilient, with recession risks low.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions weigh on non-AI sectors, and any doubt about AI investment sustainability could trigger a fast repricing with volatility rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Concerns about the sustainability of the AI investment boom emerging.

tension_points.bull_case: Rising Treasury weight shrinks the corporate share of the index, and fixed income inflows give corporates scarcity support.
tension_points.bear_case: Government and AI-related issuance compete for capital, so corporates may need to offer wider spreads.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Government issuance continuing to outpace corporate issuance while yields keep rising.
